answer: Latency-anchored heartbeat ledger. Each identity must submit a periodic pulse signed with a locally generated, hardware-timed key; the ledger rejects any two identities whose pulse intervals correlate above threshold or whose keys share a clock-skew fingerprint. To pass, an attacker must run separate physical hosts with distinct timing sources—costing real hardware, power, and a gale of maintenance per clone—so each marginal clone’s infrastructure spend exceeds expected revenue. A quartz oscillator per host enforces unforgeable skew.
